candidateEvidence: The pin mechanism is proven by five earlier dispatches (beta.36 twice, beta.37 three times). The workflow checks out this commit with BEST_AGENT_SOURCE_TOKEN, builds the linux-x64-gnu SEA with `pnpm pack:tui` + stage-cli-sea-packages.mjs on ubuntu-24.04, and freezes its own receipt (binary/tarball/staged lock/runtime lock/build report hashes) as artifact frontier-harness-candidate-<runId>. candidateDeltaAudit.method: Read-only compare of the two commits (gh api .../compare) against the argv the benchmark actually uses (headless `best-agent run --model ... --model-timeout-ms 840000 ...`, no --compact-dir, no --memory-dir). Files in the four paths audited for the previous re-pin were checked by presence in the changed-file list first, then the remaining changed files were inspected for model-visible surface.
candidateDeltaAudit.unchangedPipelinePaths: The 840s model-timeout pipeline (apps/cli/src/v3-run.ts, v3-run-options.ts, v3/plan.ts, v3/kernel/transition.ts), the prompt/context composition (v3-prompt-composition.ts, v3-context-composition.ts), the headless entry (apps/cli/src/index.ts, v3-run.ts, product-slices/thread-orchestration-root.ts) and the thread tools (v3-thread-tool.ts) are ALL ABSENT from the changed-file list: byte-identical to the beta.38 build whose 840s ceiling and transport behaviour were measured twice.
modelVisibleChanges: Instruction part (prompt-visible): composeProcess's contribution now adds 'Prefer process-start for builds, tests, installs and commands of uncertain duration. Omit lifetimeMs unless you need an intentional hard cutoff; do not use an estimated duration as [a kill deadline]' (apps/cli/src/product-slices/process.ts). The task model reads this sentence; it is the only prompt-composition change found.

Builtin workspace tools (description-only): list/stat/mkdir/remove descriptions now state their accepted key set via the spec-213 sentence (packages/capability-builtin-tools/src/index.ts). Input schemas and accepted keys are unchanged — the tools already took only `path`; only the description text is new.

Process tools (description-only): start/read/write/stop descriptions now name their own key sets, and the 30s waitMs ceiling is named by one constant shared by the canonicalizer, JSON Schema and description (packages/capability-process-tools/src/index.ts). The ceiling value itself is unchanged.

exec failure naming: a call whose cwd is missing or is not a directory is now reported as `cwd does not exist (<cwd>)` / `cwd is not a directory (<cwd>)` with the observation still `not-found`, instead of one generic not-found naming only the command (packages/workspace-tools-backend/src/index.ts). This changes a failure-path message the model can read.

Model binding window anchoring (spec 257): input-window samples now carry a history fingerprint and a session with no sample of its own anchors on the most recent report for the same history, so a fold-replacement or freshly seeded Session reuses the count that history was measured in (packages/model-binding-ai-sdk/src/index.ts). Affects window/fold decisions only; the conservative-estimate fallback is unchanged.
Subagent loop: states providerModelImageInputSupport unknown instead of inheriting a chat pair (apps/cli/src/v3-subagent-loop.ts, spec 252).
Runtime: a rejected Dim OAuth refresh keeps the persisted login instead of dropping it (apps/cli/src/runtime.ts) — robustness of the credential this run itself uses.
Thread store: SCHEMA_VERSION 52 -> 53 with migrations that keep every parent reference and child row on a legacy rebuild (spec 255).
candidateDeltaAudit.nonModelVisibleChanges: The dimsdk tree (TUI), render-core locales, tui-cpu-control, auto-compact / auto-compact-turn TUI wiring, image-models TUI, native-runtime-bridge, snapshot-to-messages presentation, scripts/pack-cli-node.mjs and scripts/dimsdk-tui.ts, docs/**, specs/** and the *.test.ts files. candidateDeltaAudit.reading: Unlike beta.37 -> beta.38 (one model-visible delta), this transition carries several small model-visible deltas: one added prompt sentence about long-running commands, self-describing key sets on the workspace and process tools, a more specific exec cwd failure message, and the window-anchoring rule. The timeout, retry and context-window mechanics that produced every measured outcome and latency figure are unchanged, so the two known failure modes (public.ecr.aws pull throttle, a first call outrunning the 840s per-call ceiling) must be re-observed rather than assumed away.
